summary: Batch C, family C2 (`perfect_matching`). The three inventory definitions `x24_perfect_matching` (cycle), `x18_perfect_matching` and `x25_perfect_matching` (packing) all read "every member is an edge and every vertex lies in exactly one member" (X18 states the edge clause through C1's `x15_matching`, now the alias of `connectivity.matching`); they now unfold to the existing `GTBase.common.perfect_matching M := matching M /\ cover M = [set: G]`, keeping their names as transparent aliases for one migration cycle. The two readings are logically equivalent without any guard (`perfect_matching_exactly_oneP`): exactly one = at most one (the matching clause) and at least one (the cover clause); on the empty graph `set0` is a perfect matching in both, a family with a non-edge member is rejected by both. Statement texts, doc blocks, manifest rows and leg states are unchanged (checked below).

Three statements are affected: X24's row through `x24_one_factorization`, X18's row through `x18_perfect_matching` (its frozen chain was already built by C1 in `Packing.migration.matching`) and X25's row through `x25_perfect_one_factorization` (its frozen chain was already built by M1 in `Packing.migration.simple_edges`; M1's copies `X25Legacy.hamiltonian_edge_set` and `cycle_edge_seq` reach no helper of this family and are convertible to the live declarations, so they are not objects of this spec). C2 preserves those frozen bodies and theorem statements, re-proves the old helper certificates `x18_perfect_matching_compat` and `x25_perfect_matching_compat` (which unfolded the exact-one incidence) through the new presentation lemma, and states this family's helper and row certificates over the same frozen bodies in its per-area entry point `Packing.migration.perfect_matching`, proved from the adapted old certificates; the statement-level certificates of C1 and M1 are unchanged. X24's chain and the pre-M1 edge set are frozen in `Cycle.migration.perfect_matching` in A1's convention.

Canonical API and grounding in common.v's perfect-matching section (narrow edits): `perfect_matching_matching`, `perfect_matching_cover`, `perfect_matching_edge`, `perfect_matching_exactly_oneP`; grounding `perfect_matching0_K0` (empty graph), `not_perfect_matching0` and `perfect_matching_K2` (existing), `not_perfect_matching_loop`, `card_perfect_matching` (`#|G| = 2 * #|M|`), `not_perfect_matching_odd` and `not_perfect_matching_K3`. The public client `base/theories/examples/perfect_matching.v` imports `GTBase.base` only and constructs a positive K4 matching with the two edges {0,1} and {2,3}, alongside its K0/K2 positive and K3 negative cases. The fidelity fragment `meta/foundation_fidelity/perfect-matching.json` enrols `perfect_matching` in `GTBase.common` with these lemmas as machine evidence; the family document is `meta/library_primitives/perfect-matching.json`.

Distinct, not claimed: `Cycle.conjectures.U10.is_perfect_matching` and `perfect_matching_cover` live on U10's multigraph edge type (`{set edge G}`, `subdeg`), a different carrier. Edge partitions (`x15_edge_partition`, X18) and edge families stay the next family.
